reason: I'd install it on a whim and poke at it, because I try everything. But FastStone already does the one thing I need, which is open my relatives' photos and print one, so I wouldn't make a new app my default for that.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers are cool and I'd want to see rapid next/back for myself, but my files are phone JPGs and screenshots and FastStone is fast enough for those. The page doesn't say anything about printing, and that's my main use. I also don't see anything for FastStone's simple editor that I use daily (resize, crop, red-eye). It's one developer on version 0.4.1, so I'd be setting it as the default for a long time with no sign of how it will be maintained.
current_app_pros: FastStone's full-screen mode with the hover toolbars, the thumbnail browser, and a simple editor for crop/resize/rotate. It's all in one app, and I know where everything is.
current_app_pains: Nothing much really. It looks a bit old and it's a little slow when I hold the arrow key through lots of photos, but I rarely notice it.
objection: I can't tell if it can print, and I don't know whether this one-person app will still be updated in a year. Neither of those is a problem I'd be taking on just for a few milliseconds of speed.
would_change_my_mind: A print dialog that works as well as FastStone's, a basic crop/resize editor, and a few months of regular updates from the developer.
